idiom_name: context key + provider scope + ambient reader with default fallback and nested override
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: create a context key with a stable identity, a provider that publishes a value for the region it encloses, a reader helper that resolves the nearest enclosing provider and falls back to a declared default, and a scope exit path that pops the binding and notifies readers. Where the platform already provides the mechanism - a component framework, thread/task-local storage, implicit parameters, an effect environment - bind to it instead of re-inventing the tree structure; where it does not, pass an explicit context object instead (see the per-language files). Nested providers must shadow the outer binding for their own scope only, and the published value should be treated as immutable with stable identity so readers can compare cheaply. For coroutine/task-scoped implementations (Python contextvars, AsyncLocal<T>, Swift actor isolation), prefer a token-based reset pattern to guarantee restoration on both normal and exceptional exit.
code_sketch:
key = create_context("theme", default = "light")

with provide(key, "dark"):        # scope: subtree / request / task
    reader()                     # nearest provider, else the default
# nested provide(key, "sepia") shadows only inside its own scope
pitfalls: A reader that no provider encloses silently takes the default; treat the missing-provider case as an error unless the default is genuinely meaningful on its own.
Rebinding the same key must restore the previous value on scope exit; a binding that leaks past its scope hands a stale value to unrelated work.
The identity of the key - and, in identity-compared runtimes, of the value - decides whether lookups and updates work at all; copying either breaks the contract.

In Python, ContextVar objects must be created at module top level, never inside a function or closure, because Context objects hold strong references that prevent garbage collection (documented in PEP 567 and Python docs).
In React Strict Mode (Development), the provider subtree renders twice; setup code with side effects must be idempotent or moved outside the render path.
In Flutter, calling InheritedWidget.of() inside build() before the widget is inserted causes an assert failure; call it in didChangeDependencies or guard with maybeOf.

In Vue, providing a reactive ref without readonly() lets injectors mutate the provider's state directly, breaking the ownership contract; always wrap with readonly() when mutation should stay in the provider.

Wrong move: establish request context with AsyncLocalStorage.enterWith(store) -> the store leaks into the caller's synchronous code and unrelated requests can read the wrong store -> instead wrap the handler in run(store, callback), which restores the previous context when the callback returns.

Wrong move: publish high-frequency state (input values, scroll position, live data) in a context consumers already subscribe to -> every keystroke re-renders the whole consumer set -> instead keep hot state in local state or a narrowly-scoped provider and publish only the slow-moving slice.

Wrong move: ship a plausible default so a missing provider never throws -> the reader silently renders the fallback value and the bug surfaces only in production or after the provider moves up the tree -> instead default to null or a sentinel and let the custom accessor throw an error naming the required provider.
sources: React documentation: Passing Data Deeply with Context - the canonical description of prop drilling, the create/provide/read steps, the use cases and the recommended alternatives (Meta Open Source; context API reshaped with React 16.3, 2018). https://react.dev/learn/passing-data-deeply-with-context
React Context API & useContext Deep Dive - real-world patterns and performance pitfalls including context splitting, memoisation, and Strict Mode double-render. https://dev.to

Vue Provide / Inject - official documentation covering provide/inject with reactive values, readonly(), Symbol keys, app-level provide, and factory-function defaults. https://vuejs.org/guide/components/provide-inject

Jetpack Compose CompositionLocal - official documentation covering static vs dynamic CompositionLocals, localOf vs compositionLocalOf, and the identity-based update model. https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/compositionlocal
Python contextvars module (PEP 567) - official docs covering ContextVar, Token-based reset, copy_context(), and native asyncio support. https://docs.python.org/3/library/contextvars.html

Flutter InheritedWidget class documentation - covering of()/maybeOf(), context descendant requirement, updateShouldNotify, and InheritedModel for partial updates. https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/InheritedWidget-class.html

SwiftUI EnvironmentValues - Apple documentation covering environment(_:), environmentObject, and the @Environment property wrapper for reading injected values. https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/environmentvalues
React Context is Dependency Injection, Not State Management - argues for restricting Context to read-mostly DI use cases and avoiding it for high-frequency state updates. https://testdouble.com
